grub: (countable) An insect at an immature stage of its life cycle.
To scavenge or in some way scrounge, typically for food.
grudge: (countable) Deep-seated and/or long-term animosity or ill will about something or someone, especially due to perceived mistreatment.
gruesome: Repellently frightful and shocking; horrific or ghastly.
grumble: (intransitive) To make a low, growling or rumbling noise, like a hungry stomach or certain animals.
(intransitive) To complain; to murmur or mutter with discontent; to make ill-natured complaints in a low voice and a surly manner.
grumbler: A person who persistently grumbles; a complainer.
grus: (constellation) A spring constellation of the southern sky, said to resemble a crane. It contains the star Alnair and lies south of the constellation Piscis Austrinus.
gta: (video games) Initialism of w:Grand Theft Auto, a series of video games by Rockstar Games involving car theft and gang warfare.
guacamole: An avocado-based greenish dip with onions, tomato, and spices, common to Mexican cuisine and often served with tortilla chips.
guadalajara: A city, the capital of Guadalajara, Spain.
guadalcanal: A volcanic island in the Pacific, part of the Solomon Islands.
guadeloupe: An archipelago, overseas department, and administrative region of France, including the island of Guadeloupe.
guadiana: A major river in Spain and Portugal.
guam: An unincorporated territory of the United States, located in the Pacific Ocean. Official name: Territory of Guam.
guanaco: A South American ruminant (Lama guanicoe), closely related to the other lamoids, the alpaca, llama, and vicuña in the family Camelidae.
guangdong: A populous province of China, located on the southern coast. Capital: Guangzhou.
guangzhou: A major prefecture-level city and port, the capital and largest city of Guangdong, in southeastern China.
guarana: A tree, Paullinia cupana, native to Venezuela and northern Brazil.
guarantee: To give an assurance that something will be done right.
guard: A person who, or thing that, protects or watches over something.
(military, often, _, in the plural) An elite military unit in Russia, the former Soviet Union and several post-Soviet countries.
A part of a machine which blocks access to dangerous parts.
guardian: Someone who guards, watches over, or protects.
(video games) A major or final enemy; boss.
guardianship: The office or position of one acting as a guardian or conservator, especially in a legal capacity.
guatemala: A country in Central America. Official name: Republic of Guatemala, a Central American country.
guava: A tropical tree or shrub of the myrtle family, Psidium guajava.
Its yellowish tropical fruit, globular or pear-shaped with thin, yellow, green or brown skin, is often made into jams and jellies.
guberniya: (historical) A major administrative subdivision of the Russian Empire; a governorate or province.
guernsey: An island, the second-largest of the Channel Islands.
guess: To reach a partly (or totally) unconfirmed conclusion; to engage in conjecture; to speculate.
To solve by a correct conjecture; to conjecture rightly.
(chiefly, US) to suppose, to imagine (introducing a proposition of uncertain plausibility).
(obsolete) To hit upon or reproduce by memory.
guesstimate: (informal) An estimate that is hardly any better than a guess, often because it is based on insufficient or unreliable data.
guest: A recipient of hospitality, especially someone staying by invitation at the house of another.
guesthouse: A small house near a main house, for lodging visitors.
guidance: The act or process of guiding.
Any process or system to control the path of a vehicle, missile etc.
guide: To serve as a guide for someone or something; to lead or direct in a way; to conduct in a course or path.
guideline: A non-specific rule or principle that provides direction to action or behaviour.
guild: A group or association mainly of tradespeople made up of merchants, craftspeople, or artisans, particularly in the Middle Ages, established to oversee and protect their specific commercial interests and to provide mutual aid.
guilder: The current currency unit in the islands of the Caribbean Netherlands, divided into 100 cents.
guillemet: Either of the punctuation marks « or » (or ‹ or ›), used in several languages to indicate passages of speech. Similar to typical quotation marks used in the English language, such as “ and ”.
guillotine: (historical, also, figuratively) A machine used for the application of capital punishment by decapitation, consisting of a tall upright frame from which is suspended a heavy diagonal-edged blade which is dropped onto the neck of the person
A device used for cutting the pages of books, stacks of paper, etc., to straight edges, usually by means of a hinged or sliding blade attached to a flat platform.
guilt: (law) The state of having been found guilty or admitted guilt in legal proceedings.
guinea: (historical) The coastal region of West Africa between Morocco and the Congo, particularly the north shore of the Gulf of Guinea.
guinea-bissau: A country in West Africa. Official name: Republic of Guinea-Bissau.
guise: A customary way of speaking or acting; a fashion, a manner, a practice (often used formerly in such phrases as "at his own guise"; that is, in his own fashion, to suit himself.)
guitar: (musical instrument) A stringed musical instrument, of European origin, usually with a fretted fingerboard and six strings, played with the fingers or a plectrum (guitar pick).
guitarfish: Any of the family Rhinobatidae of rays with elongated bodies, flattened heads and trunks, and small, ray-like wings.
gulag: (historical) Also GULAG: the system of all Soviet labour camps and prisons in use, especially during the Stalinist period (1930s–1950s).
gules: (tincture) In blazon, of the colour red.
(tincture) Red, e.g. on a coat of arms, typically represented in engraving by vertical parallel lines.
gulf: (geography) A portion of an ocean or sea extending into the land; a partially landlocked sea
gull: A seabird of the genus Larus or of the subfamily Larinae.
gully: A trench, ravine or narrow channel which was worn by water flow, especially on a hillside.
gum: (often, in the plural) The flesh around the teeth.
(botany, biochemistry, mostly, uncountable) A viscous water-soluble carbohydrate exudate of certain plants that hardens when it becomes dry, or such a substance as a component of a plant exudate.
(countable) A single piece of chewing gum.
gummi: A sugary, gelatinous material used to make candies.
gumption: (US) Boldness of enterprise; aggressiveness or initiative.
gun: (military) A cannon with relatively long barrel, operating with relatively low angle of fire, and having a high muzzle velocity.
A very portable, short firearm, for hand use, which fires bullets or projectiles, such as a handgun, revolver, pistol, or Derringer.
A less portable, long firearm that fires bullets or projectiles; a rifle, either manual, automatic or semi-automatic; a flintlock, musket or shotgun.
(informal) (gunning for something or gunning to do something) make a great effort.
gunboat: (nautical) Any of the various types of small armed vessels.
gunfire: Shots from a gun or guns, typically creating loud report.
gunk: (uncountable, informal) Grime, dirt, slime; any vague, messy, or unknown substance.
gunner: (military rank) An artillery soldier, especially one who holds private rank.
gunpowder: An explosive mixture of saltpetre (potassium nitrate), charcoal and sulfur; formerly used in gunnery but now mostly used in fireworks.
guqin: A plucked zither-like stringed instrument (chordophone), traditionally featuring seven unfretted strings, originating in ancient China.
guru: In Indian traditions: a spiritual teacher who transmits knowledge to a shishya. [from 17th c.]
gusle: (musical instrument) A single-stringed lute-like musical instrument with a bowl-shaped body, held vertically in the lap and played with a bow, originating among the Slavic peoples in the Balkans, especially in the Dinarides region.
gust: A strong, abrupt rush of wind.
(by extension) Any rush or outburst (of water, emotion, etc.).
gustation: The ability to taste flavors; the sense of taste.
gut: The alimentary canal, especially the intestine.
(informal) The abdomen of a person, especially one that is enlarged.
guts: The entrails or contents of the abdomen.
gutsy: (informal) Marked by courage, determination or boldness in the face of difficulties or danger; having guts.
gutta: (architectural element) A small water-repelling, cone-shaped projection used in the architrave of the Doric order in classical architecture.
gutter: A duct or channel beneath the eaves of a building to carry rain water; eavestrough.
guv: (UK, Irish, chiefly, London, informal) A form of address to a man, usually a stranger or a superior.
guy: (especially, in the plural, often, controversial) A person (see usage notes).
guyana: A country in South America. Official name: Co-operative Republic of Guyana. Capital and largest city: Georgetown.
gym: (especially, weightlifting) A sports facility specialized for lifting weights, cardio machines, and other exercise (culturally differentiated from sense 1).
gymnasium: (formal) A large room or building for indoor sports.
gymnast: One who performs (the sport of) gymnastics.
gymnastics: A sport involving the performance of sequences of movements requiring physical strength, flexibility, and kinesthetic awareness.
gynecology: (American spelling) The study of, or the branch of medicine specializing in, the medical problems of women, especially disorders of the reproductive organs.
gypsum: A mineral consisting of hydrated calcium sulphate. When calcinated, it forms plaster of Paris.
gypsy: (sometimes, offensive) A member of the Romani people, or one of the sub-groups (Roma, Sinti, Romanichal, etc).
(colloquial) An itinerant person or any person, not necessarily Romani; a tinker, a traveller or a carny.
gyrate: (intransitive) To revolve round a central point; to move spirally about an axis, as a tornado.
gyroscope: An apparatus composed of a wheel which spins inside of a frame (gimbal) and causes the balancing of the frame in any direction or position. In the form of a gyroscopic stabilizer, used to help keep aircraft and ships steady.
gyōda: A city in Saitama Prefecture, Japan.
